name: baseline-and-acceptance
body: Measured full-scan baselines that define the wins. jgrapht (the reference workload, fast CI baseline): full scan ~16s wall (~12s logged) — Java frontend ~9s (~70%), graph assembly ~1s, DB load ~2s, startup/overhead 3–4s; 21,334 nodes, 153k edges, 18 MB DB. netbeans (motivation only, NOT an acceptance workload): ~1h+ full scan. Acceptance — all three scenarios on jgrapht (requirements.requirement.incremental-acceptance-targets): fresh worktree near-instant; a 1–5 file localized edit materially below the recorded ~16s baseline (stated target of at most half, ~8s; frontend phase materially below the ~9s Java-frontend baseline and driven by the reduced target set, not a full frontend pass over all packages); a signature change to a widely-depended symbol may approach a full scan but must be exact (incremental graph equals a from-scratch full scan of the same changed tree). Re-measure each phase via the per-phase timing report.
